Ticket T-0014: Pin and document the PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE refusal of continuable subagents.
You are the Subagent Steward (seat `harness-core-subagent-steward`) of the `harness-core` division, working this ticket in your own git worktree on your own branch.
Task: Problem: continuable children require a session-persistence backend. `requirePersistence()` at packages/subagent/subagent/src/continuation.ts:1470-1478 throws `SubagentError` with code `PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE` and is reached from `startContinuable` (continuation.ts:403-407) and from cold continuation (`coldResume`, continuation.ts:883-889). No test in the repository asserts that code: every continuation spec composes `dsh-session-persistence` (for example packages/subagent/subagent/tests/continuation.spec.ts:189), and the README's `startContinuable` row (packages/subagent/subagent/README.md:19) and continuable-Activation section (README.md:103) never name the failure. A deployment that mounts a continuable delegation tool without a backend therefore has no documented, pinned refusal.

Required: add packages/subagent/subagent/tests/persistence-unavailable.spec.ts that composes the service with a scripted provider but without `dsh-session-persistence` (reuse the fixtures of tests/service.spec.ts or tests/continuation.spec.ts), calls `startContinuable(...)`, and asserts rejection with a `SubagentError` whose `code` is `PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE` and whose message names the backend to load, and that no child session was created and no `subagent/start` event was emitted; cover the cold-continuation entry the same way if the fixture can reach it. Document the code in the README next to `startContinuable`, English and Chinese together, then re-record with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write packages/subagent/subagent/README.md`.

Constraints: no source change beyond documentation; do not weaken the refusal into a warning. The coverage check runs the subagent packages whose tests own this package's src; until T-0020 merges, packages/subagent/subagent/tests/out-of-process.spec.ts:77 fails under uid 0 for a reason unrelated to this ticket, so run acceptance as a non-root user or after T-0020.

Ticket T-0016: Document the toolFilter value shape and its load-time validation in the tool-subagent README.
You are the Tool Subagent Steward (seat `harness-core-tool-subagent-steward`) of the `harness-core` division, working this ticket in your own git worktree on your own branch.
Task: Problem: the config table row for `toolFilter` (packages/subagent/tool-subagent/README.md:27, quoted in the source anchor) never states the value. The schema at packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts:94-97 accepts `{ allow?: string[]; deny?: string[] }`; omission is preserved on purpose because Schemastery's `{ allow: [] }` default would deny every tool (comment at index.ts:93); a `toolFilter` that names neither list is rejected at load with the message at index.ts:272-274; and the value reaches the child as a `ToolRestriction` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:691-696: `allow` keeps only the named global tools visible, `deny` removes the named ones) applied through `childCtx.tools.restrict(...)` at packages/subagent/subagent/src/child-agent.ts:174. A deployment author cannot write a valid filter from the README alone, and README.md:15 already warns that the filter is not an authority ceiling.

Required: in the config table row (and in the cordis.yml example if the README has one) document the two keys, that each is a list of global tool names, what `allow` and `deny` do as `ToolRestriction` defines them (state the precedence the tools registry implements when both are present, read from packages/core/tools/src/index.ts), that a `toolFilter` naming neither key fails load with the message at index.ts:273, and that omitting the key means no restriction. English and Chinese together, then re-record with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write packages/subagent/tool-subagent/README.md`.
